Subject: KMS / escrow requirements for no-training guarantee

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this — MedSys is running procurement on a pilot and we have a couple of tight asks from legal/security that will determine whether we can sign the DPA redline. Our primary concerns are around:

- Customer-managed KMS and key residency (we need keys that remain under our control or clear onshore key-wrapping behavior).
- A model/asset escrow option (we need a way to escrow the model binary + a short-term transcript extract if requested for audits).
- Clear evidence that requests routed to a "no-training" variant are not used for model improvement (logs, KV isolation, tagging).

Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide and the operational steps? Attached is our current DPA redline (medsys_dpa_redline_v3.pdf). Also include an architecture diagram if helpful.

Would prefer a short call tomorrow to align on what Redwood can commit to and a rough timeline for the evidence pack.

Thanks,
Sara Liu

Subject: Re: KMS / escrow requirements for no-training guarantee

Sara — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, details below and attached a simple KMS/serving diagram (kms-architecture-diagram.png).

- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via cloud KMS integrations. Keys can be resident in your region and we support onshore wrapping for tokens/exports.
- Escrow: We can offer a third-party escrow of model binaries and a time-limited audit extract. We typically work with independent escrow vendors; legal will need to approve the escrow scope.
- No-training evidence: We can provide an "evidence pack" that includes request-level routing logs, model variant configuration showing learning disabled, and operational runbooks showing KV cache isolation and prefix caching behavior.

Open questions for you:
1) Do you require escrow to be invoked only on contract breach/termination or on every audit?
2) What frequency of audit extracts (daily/weekly/monthly) would satisfy compliance?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll loop in Ops (Marissa) to list the exact artifacts and timing.
- David (infra) can scope the BYOK/HSM integration and any perf/lifecycle impacts.
- If you can confirm frequency and invocation conditions we will return a timeline (we usually turn around a standard evidence pack in ~10 business days once legal approval/credentials are provided).

Happy to take a 20-minute call tomorrow AM PST.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-02T09:50:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Internal: evidence pack checklist for MedSys

Technical notes / constraints:

- BYOK/HSM: We support cloud KMS provider BYOK (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with customer keys wrapped in an HSM. Full HSM-on-prem integration would be a separate engineering engagement.
- Onshore routing: We can route model invocations to region-specific pools and ensure that logs/audit extracts remain onshore. This requires a routing policy tied to the customer's account and explicit subnetwork rules.
- No-training gating: Operationally, we maintain a "learning" boolean at the route/model-variant level. To prove non-use for model improvement we must: 1) show config (variant.learning=false), 2) provide KV cache separation evidence, and 3) prove that training data pipelines exclude that route. We can produce logs that map request IDs to variant IDs and show no downstream training job ingestion for those IDs.
- Performance impact: Onshore key wrapping and additional routing adds ~10-30ms median latency in our benchmarking; continuous batching behavior remains unchanged. If MedSys wants per-request encryption with customer key wrapping at token-level, that adds additional CPU cost and may require a dedicated pool.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix that explains the mappings we will include in the evidence pack. Link to internal runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-medical-evidence

—David
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
